transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, what brings me in is that I just keep dodging anything that even smells like my old job. I mean office buildings, security talks, networking events anywhere near the work sites... I just avoid all of it. And if people start asking about the day it happened, I just make some excuse and get out of there. It's starting to really get in the way of things, so I figured I needed to come in.
Do you find yourself having unwanted, vivid memories or nightmares about that day at your old job?

Yes, I do. It happens out of nowhere, really. I’ll just be doing something normal, like washing the dishes, or driving past a warehouse gate, and... the scene just pops back into my head. It's so sharp. I can actually hear the panic in people’s voices, and my chest tightens up exactly like I’m right back there.
How long have you been experiencing these intrusive memories and avoidance behaviors?
Well, this has been going on since I was fired after that armed incident. So... it's been about a year and seven months now.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood or how you feel about yourself since that day, such as feeling detached from others or constantly on edge?

Yes, definitely the detached part. I mean... I still show up sometimes for family gatherings, or for mentoring, but it just doesn't feel the same. I feel like I'm sitting behind a pane of glass. I'm just sitting there, nodding along while everybody else is actually connected and together, and I'm just... somewhere else entirely.
Do you find yourself feeling constantly on edge or easily startled by sudden noises or movements?

Yes, I do. It doesn't take much, really. If a car backfires, or a door slams... or even if somebody just touches my shoulder when I don’t see them coming, I jump hard. And my heart just keeps racing long after everyone else has moved on and forgotten about it.
